**Title:** Mapping the Detectability Landscape of Iterative Model Collapse

**Abstract:** When language models train iteratively on their own output, distributional degradation proceeds silently until collapse is advanced. We map the detectability landscape of this process primarily on Pythia-410M across 13 contamination levels, with cross-architecture validation on five families (345M–6.9B parameters), revealing blind zones, sharp detection onsets, and a non-monotonic dip where Granger detection fails despite confirmed causal flow. Permutation Granger causality (PermG) identifies a detection boundary α_c(T) following a power law in observation length (leave-one-T-out CV: MAE=0.037, 15/15 cells within CI): any nonzero contamination produces signal, but sub-linear growth makes detection a function of T. This landscape is profoundly method-dependent: five statistical methods applied to identical data yield null-control false positive rates from 0% to 92%. Under mode amplification, entropy Granger-precedes diversity collapse with a ≥1-generation lag (confirmed in 14 of 15 experiments), providing a canary signal whose triggered cessation reduces peak perplexity as a proof-of-concept intervention.
